Newly hatched prolarvae of Largehead hairtail emerge from pelagic eggs at a remarkably small size, with a total length at birth of 0.5 centimeters [Lb = 0.5 centimeters]. The wet weight at birth is correspondingly minute, calculated from the mean egg diameter of 0.0933 centimeters to be 0.000425 grams [Wwb = 0.000425 grams], a value that reflects the limited yolk reserves available to the endotrophic larva before it must commence exogenous feeding. Embryonic development proceeds rapidly at the water temperatures typical of its subtropical spawning grounds; incubation at 22 °C [T = 22 °C] results in an age at birth of 3.29 days [ab = 3.29 days], a brief period that minimizes the vulnerability of the incubating egg to pelagic predators. Field observations confirm that the yolk-sac larva undergoes complete yolk absorption within a few days post-eclosion, after which the mouth opens and the onset of first feeding occurs. The tiny size at birth imposes a high risk of starvation during the exotrophic transition, as the prolarva must immediately locate suitable planktonic prey to fuel its rapid somatic growth.

Understanding the maximum reproductive output of Largehead hairtail requires coupling fecundity per spawning event with the frequency of those events. Under a thermal regime of 15 °C [T = 15 °C], adult females produce approximately 1,192 eggs per spawning event [N_R_i = approximately 1,192 eggs per spawning event], with spawning occurring daily [F_R_i = spawning occurring daily], a remarkable fecundity that is characteristic of batch-spawning teleosts with high lifetime reproductive investment. Field estimates indicate that this daily spawning frequency, maintained over the prolonged reproductive season, gives the species an enormous potential for population replenishment. At 20 °C [T = 20 °C], the gonadosomatic index (GSI) averages 4.1% [GSI = 4.1%].

The growth trajectory of Largehead hairtail is well described by a rapid juvenile phase followed by an asymptotic approach to the ultimate adult size. Individuals attain an ultimate total length of 89.6 centimeters [Li = 89.6 centimeters] and an ultimate wet weight of 5,000 grams [Wwi = 5,000 grams], making it one of the larger members of the Trichiuridae. The time from birth to the attainment of sexual maturity is approximately 183 days when reared at 20 °C [T = 20 °C], corresponding to a time since birth at puberty of 183 days [tp = 183 days]. At this developmental milestone, individuals measure roughly 12 centimeters [Lp = roughly 12 centimeters] in total length at puberty and have attained a wet weight at puberty of about 80 grams [Wwp = about 80 grams]. Maturation typically occurs between March and June, with the smallest mature individuals recorded at 13 to 14 centimeters in June, indicating a protracted spawning season during which early-spawned cohorts may reach maturity within the same year.

The total lifespan of Largehead hairtail in natural populations is approximately 15 years [am = approximately 15 years] when ambient water temperatures average 18 °C [T = 18 °C]. This extended lifespan, combined with the species' high fecundity and early maturation, classifies it as a typical r-selected strategist among marine teleosts. Growth increments are largest during the first two years, after which the rate of length increase gradually decelerates as individuals approach the asymptotic length. Tagging studies have confirmed that individuals can reach ages exceeding a decade, with the oldest documented specimens approaching the theoretical lifespan limit. The capacity for long-term reproductive output is therefore substantial, as iteroparous females may participate in multiple spawning seasons over many years, producing successive cohorts of pelagic larvae. This life-history pattern is well suited to the variable recruitment environments of the East China Sea and the Yellow Sea, where the species supports one of the most important commercial fisheries in the region.

Comparative analyses within the family Trichiuridae reveal that Largehead hairtail occupies an intermediate position in terms of both body size and life-history pace. While some congeners mature earlier and at smaller sizes, the combination of a 0.5 centimeter [Lb = 0.5 centimeter] total length at birth and an ultimate length approaching 90 centimeters reflects a substantial ontogenetic size increase of nearly two orders of magnitude. The wet weight at birth of 0.000425 grams [Wwb = 0.000425 grams] contrasts starkly with the ultimate wet weight of 5,000 grams [Wwi = 5,000 grams], representing an increase by a factor exceeding ten million that necessitates a piscivorous diet capable of sustaining the energetic demands of such rapid growth. Ecological interactions with sympatric predators and prey species shape the species' distribution, with temperature acting as a primary determinant of both spawning phenology and somatic growth rates. The species' broad thermal tolerance, from subtropical to temperate waters, underpins its wide geographic range throughout the coastal waters of the western Pacific Ocean.
